title: ReCTSi: Resource-efficient Correlated Time Series Imputation via Decoupled Pattern Learning and Completeness-aware Attentions

problem.claim: Correlated time series imputation is needed in data preprocessing, especially for incomplete sensor data.

gap.claim: Existing deep learning models for correlated time series imputation consume substantial computational resources, limiting deployment in resource-constrained settings.

contributions.claim: ReCTSi introduces a two-phase architecture for decoupled pattern learning.
Its Persistent Pattern Extraction phase uses a multi-view learnable codebook to identify and archive persistent patterns across time series for rapid inference-time retrieval.
Its Transient Pattern Adaptation phase uses completeness-aware attention modules to emphasize complete and more reliable data segments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ReCTSi achieves state-of-the-art imputation accuracy while using fewer computational resources than the leading existing model.
The authors report inference consumption of 0.004% of the FLOPs of its closest competitor.
The authors characterize ReCTSi as the currently best method for resource-limited scenarios based on its reported accuracy and resource consumption.

narrative_sequence.summary: Correlated time series imputation is important because sensor data is often incomplete.
Deep learning improves imputation by modeling temporal and spatial patterns.
The computational cost of deep models limits their use in resource-constrained settings.
ReCTSi addresses the limitation with decoupled persistent-pattern extraction and transient-pattern adaptation phases.
The authors report high imputation accuracy with substantially lower inference FLOPs than a close competitor.
